newsitem.title: BRAZIL: TESS TO SPEND 400 MLN REAL ON BRAZIL CELL PHONES.
newsitem.headline: TESS TO SPEND 400 MLN REAL ON BRAZIL CELL PHONES.

text.p: Brazilian-Swedish group Tess plans to invest 400 million reais on infrastructure and marketing in the first year of its 15-year cellular concession covering non-metropolitan Sao Paulo state, an official said.

Jose Henrique Castanheira, president of group member Airline Celular, told reporters the investment would be in addition to the 1.326 billion reais it will pay for the license to operate in B Band area No. 2. The group, which also includes Sweden's Telia and Brazil's Primave, would spend 300 million reais on line installation and other cellular telephone infrastructure and 100 million reais on marketing.

Swedish state-owned Telia holds 49 percent of Tess, while Primave owns 39 percent and Airline controls a 12-percent stake, he added. Telia holds 70 percent of Sweden's telecoms market and operates in 10 other countries, he added.

Castanheira acknowledged that rates offered by Tess were "were not much lower" than those of Telesp, the unit of Brazilian federal telecoms giant Telebras serving Sao Paulo state, but the tendency would be for them to fall.

As part of its bid, Tess offered an initial cellular telephone fee of 200 reais and a monthly subscription charge of 23 reais. Another Tess official said the rates included in the group's bid were about 15 percent cheaper than those offered by Telesp.
